newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Sept trade deficit $42 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Sept trade deficit $42 mln.

text.p: Argentina posted a $42 million trade deficit in September, compared with a $9.0 million surplus in the same month last year, the Statistics and Census Institute (INDEC) said Wednesday.
In the January-September period the country had a $515 trade surplus, down from a $1.19 billion surplus over the same period a year ago.
Exports in September were $1.92 billion, a 15 percent increase on September 1995, while imports were $1.96 billion, a 19 percent rise on the same month last year.
In the first nine months of the year Argentina sold $17.7 billion worth of goods and imported $17.19 billion.
The government expects its 1996 trade flows to balance, with both imports and exports totalling some $27 billion.
Sales to Mercosur customs union partners Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay in the January-September period were $5.57 billion, an eight percent rise from the same period last year.
Imports from Mercosur were $4.21 billion, a 23 percent increase from January-September 1995.
January-September exports to the NAFTA trade bloc comprising the United States, Canada and Mexico were $1.73 billion, an 11 percent rise, and imports $4.05 billion, a 14 percent increase.
January-September exports to European Union countries were $3.64 billion, a three percent rise, while imports totalled $4.96 billion, a 10 percent growth.
